tasks.notes: Every other number in the project is meaningless until this passes. See docs/SPEEDRUN_PLAN.md section 2.1. Code done: src/cuphead/evaluation/latency.py + scripts/latency_canary.py, unit-tested against a synthetic pair with a known injected delay (tests/test_latency.py). `--synthetic` self-test passes (experiments/latency_canary_synthetic_*.json) but is NOT evidence for this criterion -- it validates the measurement code, not the real pipeline. Still needed: `python3 scripts/latency_canary.py --real` on the machine actually running Cuphead.

tasks.title: Duplicate and dropped frame detection in the capture ring buffer
tasks.acceptance: A 10-minute capture reports zero duplicate and zero dropped frames via monotonic frame counters; the detector is unit-tested against a synthetic stream with injected gaps and repeats.
tasks.notes: Code done: src/cuphead/perception/capture.py (IntegrityTracker, content-checksum based -- see its docstring for why a duplicate is checked by content, not just index). Unit-tested against injected duplicates and drops, including a 10,000-frame clean-stream stand-in (tests/test_capture.py). Still needed: an actual 10-minute capture against the real screen-capture backend (open_screen_source) to close this for real.

tasks.title: Replay record format with frame-indexed action log
tasks.acceptance: Round-trip write/read of a 1000-frame replay preserves frames, frame-indexed actions, events, HUD ground truth, outcome, loadout and game build with 0 differences; the loader raises on a 1-frame action misalignment injected by the test.
tasks.notes: Code done: src/cuphead/memory/replay.py (ReplayWriter/ReplayReader). Alignment is checked twice: fail-fast in ReplayWriter.finalize, and again in ReplayReader.read as defense against a file corrupted after the fact. tests/test_replay.py covers the exact 1000-frame round trip and the 1-frame misalignment scenario named in this criterion.

tasks.title: CLI to record one human-play attempt as a replay
tasks.acceptance: scripts/record_session.py --synthetic produces a replay directory that reads back with 0 alignment errors and 0 capture-integrity violations; scripts/record_session.py --real captures >= 1 minute of live human play against the real screen-capture and gamepad-input backends with 0 duplicate/dropped frames.
tasks.notes: Human demonstrations are the seed data for the imitation-learning bootstrap the plan recommends before any RL or planning runs (docs/SPEEDRUN_PLAN.md section 4.4 / the pasted-in curriculum). Code done: src/cuphead/control/human_input.py (Action.from_raw normalizes raw controller state into the pruned 56-action space -- tests/test_human_input.py checks every raw-flag combination lands on a legal action) + scripts/record_session.py, wiring capture + human_input + memory.replay together. Both real-controller backends now exist: evdev on Linux and the `inputs` package on Windows, dispatched on platform.system() with lazy per-backend imports and per-OS markers in requirements.txt (`inputs; sys_platform == "win32"`), both funnelling through the same _blank_raw_state contract and Action.from_raw so Linux and Windows demonstrations are interchangeable in one replay buffer with no per-platform decoder. Test evidence: tests/test_human_input.py holds 37 test methods, 21 of which cover the Windows path (event folding and axis/button normalization, XInput y-positive-up not double-negated, d-pad hat and button paths, reader-thread liveness, non-blocking poll, fail-loud-instead-of-stale on a dead reader thread, backend selection, and no platform package bound at module import). QA CAVEAT 1: those 21 tests drive an injected fake device. Neither the evdev nor the inputs hardware path is executed by any test -- deliberate, there is no controller in CI -- so they are evidence for the normalization and threading logic ONLY, not for this task's acceptance criterion. QA CAVEAT 2: QA could not execute the suite in the session that wrote this note (no local process execution available); the reported '21 passing, 171/171 repo tests green' counts are carried from the implementing agent and are UNVERIFIED BY QA. What QA did verify statically: the file contains 37 test methods and the 21 Windows-path tests partition exactly as claimed across TestInputsBackendNormalization/TestInputsBackendReaderThread/TestBackendSelection/TestModuleImportsWithoutPlatformPackages, and the requirements.txt win32 marker is present. Re-run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests` and record the result here before this note is relied on. ACCEPTANCE STATUS: HALF-MET. The `--synthetic` clause has been smoke-tested end to end. The `--real` clause is NOT met on ANY OS -- no >= 1-minute live human recording against the real screen-capture and real gamepad backends has been performed on Linux or Windows, so there are zero duplicate/dropped-frame counters to attach. Adding the Windows backend closed a code-side portability gap; it did not advance the acceptance criterion by a single line of evidence. Status stays IMPLEMENTED and cannot move to VALIDATED until a real session is recorded and its integrity counters are pasted here. Also still placeholders: HUD and event logging, pending perception-hud-templates / perception-event-detector.
